correctness.rationale: For the three one-output neighborhoods 000, 011 and 110, a trace walk with a distinguished first site has exactly one valid time history for each state fixed by F^t; neither spatial shifts nor temporal starts are quotiented in that trace. Periods dividing six are 1,2,3,6, so subtraction of the two proper maximal-divisor fixed sets and addition of their intersection, followed by division by six, gives the primitive orbit number. The formal log-determinant derivative therefore has the stated signs and factor of 1/6. Independently built the time-column graph by mask arithmetic and recomputed every determinant with exact characteristic polynomials (`python3 /workspace/checks/rule73.py`, SymPy 1.14). Cyclic sizes matched [4], [8,1,1], [19], [23,8,8,8,1,1]; exact matrix powers recovered c_8=4, zeros at 1–7 and 9–11, and 12,13,14,45,116 at 12–16. A separate reachability calculation confirms a return from pair (0,21) of each length 12–23 visiting a least-period-three column; the start contains a period-two column. Their coexistence forbids every proper divisor of six, and concatenation with length-12 returns fills all larger n. Checked the indicated length-3 and length-4 cycles in the strongly connected 23-component, giving primitivity. Its determinant is (1+z²)(1+z+z²)²(1−z+z³)²E(z); exact positive-vector ratios enclose its radius in (1.61574,1.61576), hence its positive reciprocal in (.61,.63) where the other factors are nonzero. All other six-return cyclic components have radius one and the lower-time maxima are below 1.546. Trace asymptotics thus have coefficient one before division by six. The arithmetic certificates establish the finite graph facts; the bijection, concatenation and Perron argument establish the infinite claims. Frozen code and logs were read as evidence, not run.

value.rationale: Six is the first return time combining the previously studied two and three clocks. Counting their genuinely mixed primitive orbits rather than all fixed states is a natural invariant. An explicit generating series with a separate growth exponent gives counts on every indexed ring, and the mixed-clock return walks explain precisely why the four-orbit first appearance is followed by a gap before permanent support. The result is more than replaying finite spectrum tables and does not claim anything about basins or other periods.
